source_basis: NCCP 00702 v2 and current EMA Rozlytrek product information 4.2–4.6; source checked 2026-10-29. Adult ROS1 and NTRK settings remain separate.

risks.label: Thinking, memory, dizziness and driving
risks.detail: Cognitive or balance changes can affect daily life and driving; report changes promptly. Severe effects may require interruption or stopping.

risks.label: Heart failure and heart-rhythm changes
risks.detail: Breathlessness, swelling, palpitations or fainting require urgent assessment; ECG/electrolyte and risk-based heart-function checks matter.

risks.label: Liver injury and low blood counts
risks.detail: Blood tests can detect liver or blood-count effects before symptoms; jaundice, fever or marked weakness needs prompt advice.

risks.label: Fractures and visual disturbance
risks.detail: Report focal bone pain, changed gait and visual symptoms promptly.

risks.label: Raised uric acid, kidney-test changes, swelling and weight gain
risks.detail: Monitoring and symptom treatment may be needed.

risks.label: Taste change, nausea, constipation and diarrhoea
risks.detail: Symptoms can affect eating and hydration; use prescribed support and report severe symptoms.

risks.label: Pregnancy, contraception and breastfeeding
risks.detail: Avoid pregnancy. Women who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least five weeks afterwards; add a barrier method if using systemic hormonal contraception. Men with partners who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least three months afterwards. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Discuss fertility and family plans before starting.

risks.label: Medicine, food and formulation interactions
risks.detail: Give the team a complete medicine and supplement list, including St John’s wort. CYP3A inhibitors/inducers and medicines affecting heart rhythm need pharmacy review. Do not change the cancer dose yourself; temporary interaction doses differ from toxicity reductions. Swallowing difficulties require pharmacy-directed formulation instructions.
